# Current Reality and Gaps

The Awtsmoos renews every frame, every vessel, every way; Awtsmoos.com can make one movie language truthful while every studio keeps its own display.

## What exists now
- `apps/shared/movie` is the strongest canonical candidate and is modular.
- It models 2D shapes/text/paths/charts/particles/characters/groups and 3D models/characters/particles/lights/worlds.
- It models semantic cameras, transitions, keyframes, cast, assets, scenes, format and handoff metadata.
- It has a prompt-intent parser, structured intent compiler, canvas proof renderer, runtime samplers and a mobile dock.
- Animator, Nesher, Video Editor and Mitzvah Studio have adapters targeting this shared movie area.
- A three-minute canonical example and separate Animator long-movie proofs exist.

## Concrete defects observed today
1. The canonical movie directory is still entirely untracked in Git.
2. Shared-core tests are essentially absent; most movie smoke tests still live under Animator.
3. `MoviePromptIntent.js` exists but is not exported from `apps/shared/movie/index.js`; the public import smoke test fails.
4. `AiMovieContract.js` reads `MovieCapabilities.protocol`, but the current capability facade exposes `for()` and `all()`, so the contract protocol can become undefined.
5. `MovieValidator.js` checks scene range and layer start, but not layer end, keyframe bounds, camera kinds, transition kinds, duplicate cast IDs, asset references or semantic payload validity.
6. `MovieProtocol.js` still uses compact inline object formatting and truthy defaults such as `input.duration || 0`, which can hide intent and makes evolution harder.
7. The mobile `MovieDock` is primarily a JSON textarea with two buttons; it is not yet a true AI directing UX.
8. There are two Animator movie adapter implementations (`src/movie` and `src/sharedMovie`), creating ambiguity about the authoritative bridge.
9. App adapters preserve the canonical movie differently; not all return the same projection/fidelity report shape.
10. The shared layer vocabulary has no first-class audio, dialogue, video/media, mask, matte, camera-track, adjustment, subtitle or data-source layer kinds.
11. Search found no meaningful shared support for physics, collision, undo/redo, collaboration, migrations, serialization APIs, WebGPU, OffscreenCanvas, render queues or caching.
12. Character semantics are still shallow compared with the desired film-director model: no canonical skeleton, pose track, gaze, emotion, lipsync, blocking, wardrobe or continuity contract.
13. 3D rendering in the shared canvas is a proof renderer, not a full spatial renderer with true depth, materials, shadows and post-processing.
14. Cross-app round-trip editing is not defined: projection mostly flows canonical -> app, without app -> canonical reconciliation.
15. There is no canonical project diff/patch language for an AI to safely revise one scene, character or keyframe without regenerating the entire movie.
16. No canonical asset provenance, licensing, hashing, proxy/original relationship or offline availability model exists.
17. No performance budget or adaptive quality contract exists for mobile devices.
18. No accessibility contract exists for captions, audio description, color contrast, motion reduction or reading order.
19. No deterministic render acceptance suite proves the same movie remains semantically consistent across all adapters.
20. No single canonical documentation page currently tells future agents which movie core is authoritative and which old prototypes are compatibility-only.
